title: Reality Fracture Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Devourer of the Obzedat, tithe-drinker, and necroparun eternal.
She seized the throne to protect her family first, Kamigawa second.
An alloy of curiosity and hope; the caretaker of a gleaming plane of possibility.
"The Theorist swears this Multiverse will be free of suffering, but part of me wonders if he just plans on hiding it better." —Tam, field notes
"There is a deep sadness here . . . one I had not thought possible in this reality. Is it my understanding that's flawed or the Theorist's?" —-Tam, field notes
"Everything is in progress . . . just like us. May we always know exactly who we are." —Jace, to Tam
Jace could see the sunlight in his Multiverse, but somewhere along the way, he lost the feel of its warmth.
The pinnacle of Jace's hope for a better, different Multiverse.
"Jace's world is like a warped mirror. Like some part of him strains against what the Theorist is creating." —Vraska
"Captain, your units are the tip of our spear. There is zero room for failure." —Jirina Kudro
The roar of applause drowned out the melee raging in the lobby.
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.
Their war forgotten, the nations of Bant stood united in the face of a common threat.
"The Shifting Wastes provide our clan eternal protection. It is our duty to return the favor." —Kadri, Dromoka warrior
Where swords fail, faith transcends.
"Who was that knight, so graceful and strong? Why did she flee before the food was gone?" —*Tale of the Masked Maiden*
"Let the light scour away your imperfect flesh." —Heliod
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
"I have a plan. Actually, I have three."
In the Cosmos, secrets swirl and spark like windborne embers, and only Alrund can capture them.
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
In a single unending moment, a hundred lifetimes of knowledge coursed through his unraveling mind.
To Jin-Gitaxias, perfection is not a goal, but a process.
Malice spreads on wings of tyranny.
Liliana whispered to whatever consciousness Oketra and Bontu had left. "You are the gods. He is the usurper. You know what to do."
As Narset struggled to meditate, tiny dragonlings spiraled around her, conjuring thoughts of ancient clans.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
"Good ideas don't take time. They take a lot of bad ideas first." —Ral Zarek
"As Terisiare's mines ran dry, scrap metal became increasingly plentiful." —*The Antiquities War*
After years of silence, the caves once again echo with the grisly sounds of Phyrexians preparing for war.
The sunlight falls pristine on the temple at Epityr, softened by the remembered shadows of angelic saviors' wings.
None can tell how many vessels are tangled up on the sea floor—or how much treasure remains unclaimed.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
Beyond Valley lies danger—and promise.
"Do not linger in such places, child. There the gwyllions dance. If they find you, you will join in their revels for eternity." —Talara, elvish safewright
Ships blown north in their voyage across the Stormwreck Sea become trapped in the unmelting ice.
Serra's blessing lies strongest upon Sursi, where her holy chapels are untouched even as evil encroaches.
"I swear, for every one Prossh devours, three more pop out of a hole somewhere." —Jaya Ballard
The gate of every kithkin doun is a cunning trap, intended to spill visitors into an oubliette from which there is no escape.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
"The Tapestry weaves worlds on its own. All we do is tend to the process." —Antioxa, Drix elder
The boiling seas around Shiv provided a welcome layer of protection for the reclaimed Mana Rig.
"We have inherited the mysteries of the Thran, but few of the answers." —Jhoira
Everything is flammable in the Burning Isles, even the mana itself.
Without the care of the tideshapers, the Lanes lie neglected. Some have flooded entire towns; others dried to cracked mud.
"The war polluted the land, turning what had once been fruitful fields into fetid morasses of mud and rusted corpses." —*The Antiquities War*
Unconnected to the land, it hungers.
"She binds them to do naught but worship her. It is no salvation she grants, but servitude." —Geist of Saint Thalia
In the gleam between metal and suns, Memnarch found meaning.
"I knew this Multiverse to be superior when I had never experienced the other. Now that I have, I am . . . less certain." —Tam, field notes
"There is a deep sadness here . . . one I had not thought possible in this reality. Is it my understanding that's flawed or the Theorist's?" —Tam, field notes
